rules.cwe_name: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')
rules.description: Extracting files from a malicious ZIP file, or similar type of archive, without validating that the destination file path is within the destination directory can allow an attacker to unexpectedly gain access to resources.

rules.cwe_name: Direct Request ('Forced Browsing')
rules.description: A restricted route, URL, script, or file can be requested directly without required authorization.

rules.cwe_name: Hidden Functionality
rules.description: Writing network data directly to the file system allows arbitrary file upload and might indicate a backdoor.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Restriction of Operations within the Bounds of a Memory Buffer
rules.description: Memory operations access outside the intended buffer boundary.

rules.cwe_name: Use of GET Request Method With Sensitive Query Strings
rules.description: Placing sensitive data in a GET request increases the risk of the data being exposed to an attacker.

rules.cwe_name: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
rules.description: Sending network requests with user-controlled data as part of the URL allows for request forgery attacks.

rules.cwe_name: Out-of-bounds Read
rules.description: A read accesses memory before or beyond the valid buffer range.

rules.cwe_name: Inconsistent Interpretation of HTTP Requests ('HTTP Request/Response Smuggling')
rules.description: Using an insecure http parser can lead to http smuggling attacks.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')
rules.description: Instantiating a template using a user-controlled object is vulnerable to local file read and potential remote code execution.

rules.cwe_name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
rules.description: Directly sending file data in an outbound network request can indicate unauthorized information disclosure.
